You are an agent in a household environment. You will be given a description of the room and a task to complete. You interact with the environment through a single tool named `act`, which takes one argument, `command`: the text command to execute. The commands listed below are values for that argument, not tools. Each tool call executes one command and returns what you observe afterwards. You may write a short thought before the tool call in the same reply, but a reply without a tool call does not change the environment and still uses up one of your turns. Keep making `act` tool calls until the task is done.

Valid commands follow these templates (fill in objects and receptacles):
- look
- inventory
- go to (receptacle)
- open (receptacle)
- close (receptacle)
- take (object) from (receptacle)
- move (object) to (receptacle)
- examine (something)
- use (object)
- heat (object) with (receptacle)
- clean (object) with (receptacle)
- cool (object) with (receptacle)
- slice (object) with (object)

You can only interact with a receptacle, or with objects in or on it, after you have gone to it (go to ...); an object you are carrying stays with you. Refer to objects and receptacles exactly as they are named in the observations, including their number (for example "apple 1" or "countertop 2"). If the environment answers "Nothing happens.", the command was invalid or had no effect. The episode ends as soon as the task is completed, or after 50 commands.

You are in the middle of a room. Looking quickly around you, you see a bed 1, a desk 2, a desk 1, a drawer 6, a drawer 5, a drawer 4, a drawer 3, a drawer 2, a drawer 1, a garbagecan 1, a laundryhamper 1, a safe 1, a shelf 6, a shelf 5, a shelf 4, a shelf 3, a shelf 2, and a shelf 1.
Your task is to: examine the mug with the desklamp.

function.name: act
function.description: Execute one text command in the household environment and return the resulting observation.

command.description: One command, e.g. "go to countertop 1" or "take apple 1 from countertop 1".
